payload.title: Resume Papyrus MCP consent automatically after normal sign-in
payload.description:
## Intent

Apply DataParade's sign-in-first experience to the existing Papyrus MCP OAuth routes. Users see the client and publication, authenticate when needed, and approve once. PPY-fdf150 is the behavioral contract. Local work can begin with a fake provider while the audience gate is being implemented.

## Steps

1. Extend lib/mcp/oauth-http.ts, lib/mcp/oauth-site.ts and the existing /mcp/authorize route. Keep /api/mcp, its issuer and protected-resource metadata, exact registered client callbacks, the existing no-secret public client, S256, resource binding, state and iss. Preserve normal clean browser routes. Validate the initial request before creating state.
2. Persist one ten-minute encrypted pending request in the private grant service with immutable client, redirect, resource, challenge and host state. Send only an opaque browser-bound pending handle in a Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Lax host-only cookie. Use independent unpredictable values for provider OAuth state, nonce, PKCE and the same-origin consent CSRF check. Match browser, site, pending record and role at every step. Use a fixed return to /mcp/authorize. User-controlled return paths and cross-origin cookie forwarding are forbidden.
3. Use the site's normal staff sign-in for the short-window path and the existing Prospectus sign-in callback for reader sessions. Start and finish sign-in in the same tab. Use an existing valid identity where appropriate. The renewable staff path redirects via the reviewed MCP Cognito client and /mcp/callback and checks the returned subject against an existing newsroom identity when present. The final consent page shows the actual verified identity and a single Allow/Deny. If both identities are available, the choice is explicit and the grant only uses the chosen identity. Never fall through from one identity to the other.
4. Escrow any provider credentials only in the private encrypted pending record with the same ten-minute deadline. Consume provider completion and consent once. Denial clears pending state and discards or attempts to revoke the pending upstream grant. Approval moves the pending credentials into the durable grant and issues only the MCP code. Use the existing form Origin/CSRF checks and verified exact callback behavior. Return a visible resume/expired/declined/error page with no raw provider errors, tokens or query logging.
5. Keep same-origin reader consent and original Prospectus expiry. Split-origin reader work stays PPY-17cdb1. No new permission or tool changes. Update edge/consumer route and packaged-app forwarding docs for /mcp/callback only as needed.

## Gherkin acceptance

Feature: Continue sign-in and approve one connection
Scenario: A signed-out staff member accepts in the same tab
  Given the host has started a valid authorization request
  When the member signs in and returns to consent
  Then the member can approve once and the browser reaches the registered host callback
  And the host code can be redeemed only with the original PKCE verifier

Scenario: An attacker changes the sign-in flow
  Given a pending connection in one browser
  When a different browser, an expired cookie or a foreign origin tries to complete it
  Then no code is issued and the authorized browser sees a safe way to restart

Scenario: The member declines the connection
  Given the verified identity is shown for a pending connection
  When the member denies it
  Then the host gets access_denied at its exact callback
  And no MCP grant is active

## Verification

Extend features/mcp/oauth.feature, scripts/test-mcp-oauth-http.ts and scripts/test-mcp-oauth-browser.ts. Exercise real browser redirect and cookies locally without a visible Mac UI, including the earlier form-action regression. Headless fixture proof and real ChatGPT proof are recorded separately.
